text: Transferable means able to be moved from one job or place to another and still be useful. Here, skills from clay-pigeon shooting could help soldiers with a different job: stopping drones.
Proficiency is being really good at something because you have practiced it a lot. Here, the army wants soldiers to get better and better at shotguns.
To mimic is to copy how something looks, sounds or moves. Here, launchers copy the way birds fly.
A clay pigeon is a flat clay disc that is flung into the air as a moving target for shooting practice. It is called a pigeon because it flies a bit like a bird.
Clays is short for clay pigeons, the clay discs that shooters aim at.
A massacre is the killing of many people or animals. Here the writer jokes: the clay discs were not alive, but so many were smashed that it felt like one.
Wiltshire is a county in the south-west of England, where the army's shooting championship was held.
A championship is a contest to find the best player or team in a sport.
A quadcopter is a small flying machine with four spinning propellers. Many drones are quadcopters.
A drone is a flying machine with no pilot inside. It is flown by someone on the ground or by a computer.
Warfare means the way wars are fought, including the weapons and tactics used.
The Defence Investment Plan is the British government's plan for what to spend on the army, navy and air force. In June it set aside £750m for protection against drones.
Committed can mean promised to spend or do something. Here the government promised £750m, which is about 950 million dollars. It can also mean being devoted to a cause.
Counter-drone means used against drones. Counter-drone protection means ways to spot, stop or destroy enemy drones.
An acoustic radar finds things by the sounds they make. A drone's buzzing propellers can give it away.
Direct-energy weapons, such as lasers, destroy targets with a beam of energy instead of a bullet.
Futuristic means like something from the future, very modern and high-tech.
Victorian means from the time of Queen Victoria, who ruled Britain from 1837 to 1901. Here it means old-fashioned, because shotguns are old technology.
Aerial means in the air.
Shells here are shotgun cartridges, the tubes that hold the charge and the metal balls. They have nothing to do with seashells or egg shells.
Projectiles are things that are shot or thrown through the air, such as bullets or pellets.
A propeller is a set of spinning blades that pushes a drone, plane or boat along. If you damage one, the drone cannot fly well.
A crack shot is someone who is extremely good at shooting. Here, crack also describes the shooters in the title: top-quality, expert.
Tutoring means teaching one person or a small group, one-on-one.
To retrain is to teach someone again, from the start, a new way of doing something they already do differently.
Doomed means certain to fail or have a bad ending. Here, shooting a shotgun while standing stiff and still will make you miss.
Airborne means flying or in the air.
Feasibly means in a way that could really work. Here, launchers can realistically act like drones.
Mph means miles per hour, a measure of speed. 50mph is about 80 kilometres an hour.
The front line is the place where the fighting happens in a war.
A last resort is the thing you only do when everything else has failed. Here, a shotgun is the final defence if a drone gets very close.
Range here means the distance a weapon can reach. A drone within range is close enough to be hit.
To down a drone means to bring it down out of the sky.
Armoured means covered in strong protective metal to stop damage. An armoured drone is harder to shoot down.
Lead shells are shotgun shells filled with balls of lead, a heavy, soft metal.
Tinted goggles are eye protection with coloured lenses. Here the colour makes the orange discs stand out against the grey sky.
Don here is a verb meaning to put on clothing or gear. It is not the name Don.
To make something pop means to make it stand out clearly so it is easy to see.
Whizzier means faster and zippier. Whizz is the sound of something rushing by.
To identify something is to work out what it is or to spot it.
Nerds here means people who love going deep into technical details. The writer is saying the fine details are for experts.
Technique is the way you do something skillfully, such as how you stand and move when shooting.
A correspondent is a journalist who reports on a topic. Here, the writer is talking about themself.
A natural is someone who seems to be good at something without having to work at it.
If spirits are high, people are in a happy and cheerful mood.
A cloud hanging over something means a worry that spoils the good mood. The joke is that it was a misty, rainy day, but the real cloud was not the weather.
Troops are soldiers.
To sigh is to let out a long breath, often because you are tired, sad or annoyed.
Embarrassing yourself means doing something that makes you feel silly in front of others.
A hobby is an activity you do for fun in your spare time.
Aim is how well you point something at a target. To improve your aim is to hit what you are trying to hit more often.
Fighter pilots fly fast military planes that fight other aircraft.
Targets here are the things a soldier tries to hit or destroy. Drones are behind 80% of those destroyed by Ukraine.
Ukraine is a country in eastern Europe that has been fighting a war with Russia since 2022. Its army uses lots of drones.
Instructors are teachers who show people how to do something.
Shot here means the tiny metal balls inside a shotgun shell. In sports, a shot is a single attempt. And to shoot is to fire.
A rifle is a long gun that fires a single bullet very accurately over long distances.
A shotgun is a gun that fires many tiny metal balls at once, which spread out.
Launchers are machines that fling the clay discs into the air at set speeds and angles.
To simulate something is to copy it closely for practice or testing.
